## Before submitting

- [ ] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

Tests only: `test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_backward_{fp8,mxfp8}.py`.

## Summary

#1522 added `test_{fp8,mxfp8}_dense_tail_backward_is_finite_and_quantizes_bitwise` for the dense `S % 128 != 0` record that #1520 serves. That test checks finite gradients and the bitwise quantizer / scalar / delta layer. It does not compare gradient values with an oracle (CodeRabbit's nitpick on #1522).

This PR adds the same `s992_dense_b1` cell to the parametrization of `test_{fp8,mxfp8}_stage_localised_bounds`. That test checks every stage and the end gradients against the row reference and the seeded oracle, under the bounds the matrix cells use. The cell stays out of `_CELLS`, so the other matrix tests and `test_the_matrix_declares_what_the_module_says` are unchanged.

## Related issues

Follow-up to #1522 / #1520.

## API and compatibility impact

None (tests only).

## Testing

- Collection on B200: the new ids `test_{fp8,mxfp8}_stage_localised_bounds[s992_dense_b1-norm]` collect, and `test_the_matrix_declares_what_the_module_says` passes in both files.
- The new cells need SM107. CI's `python/*/cutedsl:cutlass-4.8:sm107` lane is their first run. If a stage misses its bound on the dense tail, that is a finding about the #1520 backward path.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed both changed files at `9bda7152`; no actionable findings. The new dense-tail cells reuse the existing stage-localized oracle assertions without changing tolerances or expanding the other test matrices. Integration onto `3f8348b1` is clean.

Independent SM107 validation: **6 passed, 0 skipped**—both new `s992_dense_b1-norm` stage-oracle cases, both existing dense-tail finite/bitwise tests, and both matrix-inventory checks. The stage tests assert GEMMs against FP64 products, attention gradients against their row references, and downstream gradients against an oracle seeded with the measured attention gradients. The largest reported downstream gradient-bound fractions were 0.706 for FP8 and 0.708 for MXFP8; neither had any `dW_qkvg` rows outside the existing bound. This is stage-localized validation, not a new unseeded end-to-end oracle.

The reported tuple/list collection issue does not reproduce: `_both` returns a list, and the parenthesized list additions leave `_CELLS` as a list in both modules. Both modules collected and executed successfully.

Local SM107 uses a different compiler build from CI. The owner's initial CI request failed before launching a pipeline; that is pending CI coverage, not a test failure.

<!-- codex-fe-review:github-only:vedaanta:1524:9bda71529f1b6e76510dbec40ab9cf7fd11db2a9:complete -->

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `9bda71529f1b` against base `3f8348b149bb`.

No actionable findings. The new cells enter the existing numerical assertions without changing tolerances or the other test matrices. Auto-FE: KEEP — finish this bounded coverage addition and merge once existing CI requirements are met. It closes the specific finite-but-wrong-gradient gap identified in #1522; there is no need to expand the rest of the matrix in this PR. Preserving the existing independent approval.

Validation: Reviewed both changed files and traced the stage-localized assertions: GEMMs against FP64 products, attention gradients against their row references, and downstream gradients against the oracle seeded with separately checked attention gradients. The new parametrization leaves _CELLS and its other consumers unchanged. Independent exact-head native SM107 sensitivity probe: both new dense-tail stage-oracle functions passed on unmodified results. Then, reusing one computed result per family, I independently zeroed each of dh, dW_qkvg, dW_o, dW_q_norm, dW_k_norm and attention dQ. All 12 finite-error controls raised the intended numerical/consistency assertions; each buffer was restored after its control. This confirms the added coverage is not only checking finiteness. Reused Vedaanta's six passing SM107 pytest cases for collection, the two numerical cells, the prior bitwise cells and matrix inventory. Also confirmed _CELLS is a list in both imported modules; the reported tuple/list collection failure is not present on this head. Tests-only change, so no runtime performance benchmark. Current-head CI pipeline 72720596 is already running after the peer's retry of the failed initial trigger; no duplicate CI started.

Limitations: This adds stage-localized numerical coverage, not a new unseeded end-to-end oracle or a complete dense-tail shape sweep. The mutation controls deliberately corrupt completed output buffers; they test assertion sensitivity, not a simulated defect in every possible production stage. CI remains pending.

Comment only: GitHub does not allow reviewing one's own PR with approval/request-changes.
